Glossary of Local Government Terms

Plain-language definitions for legal, policy, and planning terms commonly used across Olympia and Thurston County public dockets.

Local Legislation

Ordinance

A formal local law adopted by a city council or board of county commissioners that has permanent legal force within that city or county.

Council Action

Resolution

A formal statement of policy, administrative approval (such as accepting a grant or setting an advisory goal), or official direction that generally carries less permanent legal effect than an ordinance.

Meeting Procedure

Consent Agenda

A group of routine, non-controversial agenda items passed together in a single collective vote without separate discussion, unless a councilmember or commissioner asks to pull an item for individual debate.

Public Finance

Assessment

A fee or charge placed directly on real property tax statements for a dedicated public purpose or service, such as conservation district operations, diking districts, or stormwater management.

Environmental Review

SEPA Checklist

A standard disclosure form under the Washington State Environmental Policy Act (RCW 43.21C) where project sponsors and local agencies evaluate potential impacts on air, water, land, and traffic before permits are granted.

Growth Management

Critical Areas Ordinance (CAO)

Local land use regulations required by state law (RCW 36.70A) that establish protective buffer zones around wetlands, streams, fish and wildlife habitat conservation areas, and steep slopes.

Public Health

Group B Water System

A small public drinking water system that provides water to 2 through 14 service connections and fewer than 25 people per day, regulated primarily under county health sanitary codes (Article III).

Inter-Agency Agreement

Interlocal Agreement (ILA)

A legally binding contract between two or more local government bodies (such as between the City of Olympia and Thurston County) authorized under chapter 39.34 RCW to coordinate shared services, facilities, or funding.

Public Participation

Public Hearing

A formal meeting required by state statute or city charter where members of the public are legally entitled to give verbal or written testimony on the official record before elected officials vote on an ordinance or major land use decision.

Legal Procedure

Quasi-Judicial Action

A proceeding where elected officials or a hearing examiner act like judges applying established legal criteria to a specific property or permit application, with strict rules preventing private discussions outside the formal public record.
